01 / THE BENCHMARK

One request.
Many ways to get it wrong.

Local search combines facts, experiences, mandatory requirements, and preferences. ATLAS makes each one explicit—and verifiable.

TWO INDEPENDENT DIMENSIONS

Not every constraint
plays by the same rules.

Hard requirements must hold. Soft preferences permit disclosed trade-offs. Either can be objective or subjective.

↳

Select a constraint to explore
how it is checked.

OBJECTIVESUBJECTIVE
EVIDENCE / STRUCTURED ATTRIBUTES

Check the recorded opening hours against the query timestamp. A closed place—or an unsupported opening-hours claim—cannot satisfy this hard requirement.

01

Grounded in search events

Real logged intents are expanded with POI evidence and persona-guided requirements. Added constraints are synthesized.

02

Evidence for every requirement

Annotations connect constraints to attributes, reviews, relations, and verification criteria.

03

More than one valid answer

The engaged reference POI is not a unique ground truth. Any evidence-supported candidate can qualify.

02 / FROM LOGS TO EVALUATION

Built on evidence.
Tested in ATLASBox.

A fixed knowledge base and shared tool interfaces give every evaluated agent the same search environment.

A

Ground

Link search events to structured place attributes and review evidence; process privacy-sensitive fields.

B

Generate & refine

Prepare → Generate → Assert → Debate → Fix → Finalize. Failures inform later assertion checks.

C

Search & evaluate

Agents receive a query, timestamp, and location. Answers, tool trajectories, and resource use are assessed.

FOUR TOOLS.
ONE SHARED SANDBOX.search_poissearch_nearbysearch_notesget_poi_notes
425,244POIs with attributes & geography
260,757user notes in the frozen corpus

Shared retrieval stackQwen3 embeddings → exact FAISS search → Qwen3 reranker. Structured records are served from SQLite.

ATLAS-Bench model performance, 14 configurations

Read the metrics together. CSR and CR score returned recommendations; Success@k also counts empty answers as failures on satisfiable queries. These measures have different denominators.

05 / A BUILDING BLOCK FOR PLANNING

Small searches.
Longer consequences.

A plan supplies the location, time, and budget for local search. Retrieved candidates and their evidence can then inform the next planning decision.

CASE STUDY · QWEN3.8-MAX

A day out in Chaoyang.

The paper compares a whole-itinerary execution with seven stage-specific requests. The stage-wise responses provide more concrete detail, but CSR falls from 77.8% to 57.8%, and the factuality check fails because of grounding errors.

A single illustrative case—not an estimate of end-to-end planning success. It shows why richer plans still need reliable local verification.

01 / SET UP

Prepare the environment & corpus

Start with the source repository and its Git LFS data. Use Python ≥3.9. Retrieval runs on CPU, CUDA, or Apple Silicon MPS; a GPU is recommended.

Get the code and data from the GitHub repository ↗. The LFS command below applies to a Git checkout; for a ZIP download, verify that the actual index files are included.
SHELL / macOS & Linux
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r requirements-vector.txt

# Fetch the frozen indexes in a Git checkout
git lfs install
git lfs pull

# Fetch and verify the pinned retrieval models
python scripts/fetch_models.py
python scripts/fetch_models.py --check
Windows PowerShell setup +
POWERSHELL
py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements-vector.txt
git lfs install
git lfs pull
python scripts/fetch_models.py
python scripts/fetch_models.py --check

The evaluation shell scripts below require Bash (for example, WSL). The core agent and retrieval tools are Python.

~4.1 GB retrieval indexes~2.3 GB model weights1024-d embeddings
Verify your setup & try the search tools +
SHELL
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python scripts/check_neural_models.py
python scripts/run_tool.py search_pois '{"query":"咖啡厅","top_k":3}'
python scripts/run_tool.py search_nearby '{"query":"咖啡厅","loc":{"lng":116.46,"lat":40.0},"distance_m":2000,"top_k":5}'
02 / CONNECT

Bring your own model

Use an API endpoint or a local vLLM server. Replace the placeholders with your endpoint and model ID; credentials stay in your shell environment.

SHELL / API CONFIGURATION
export LOCAL_LIFE_API_BASE='https://your-host.example/v1'
export LOCAL_LIFE_API_KEY='<your-api-key>'
export LOCAL_LIFE_MODEL='<model-id>'
export LOCAL_LIFE_API_STYLE='chat_completions'
SHELL / LOCAL vLLM
# Start the model server in a separate terminal
vllm serve /path/to/model --port 8001

# Configure the benchmark client
export LOCAL_LIFE_API_BASE='http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1'
export LOCAL_LIFE_API_KEY='local-vllm'
export LOCAL_LIFE_MODEL='<served-model-name>'
export LOCAL_LIFE_ENABLE_THINKING='false'
export LOCAL_LIFE_THINKING_FIELD='chat_template_kwargs'

On PowerShell, use $env:NAME='value' in place of export NAME='value'. See .env.example ↗ for reasoning controls and other supported API styles.

03 / EXECUTE

One query. Then the full benchmark.

Start small, inspect the tool trajectory, then run all 1,200 inputs. Re-running the same command resumes by skipping completed task IDs.

SHELL / RUN & FINALIZE
# Your first trajectory
python scripts/run_agent.py --limit 1 --workers 1 --output outputs/first.jsonl

# Smoke test: inspect 10 trajectories
python scripts/run_agent.py --limit 10 --workers 1 --fresh --output outputs/smoke.jsonl

# Full benchmark; repeat this command to resume
python scripts/run_agent.py --workers 4 --output outputs/my_model.jsonl

# Deduplicate records and generate the summary
python scripts/finalize_run.py --input outputs/my_model.jsonl

Each JSONL record includes the final answer, tool observations, programmatic grounding checks, protocol corrections, latency, and token usage.

04 / EVALUATE

Assess the answer and the path to it.

Evaluation combines a blind constraint audit, deterministic checks, LLM judgments, and run telemetry. The constraint audit requires adjudicated verdicts before aggregation.

Answer quality · CSR, CR & Success@k +

Build blind inputs, adjudicate each chunk according to RUBRIC.md ↗, then score the verdicts.

SHELL / CONSTRAINT AUDIT
python judge/build_qoder_judge_inputs.py --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model

# Adjudicate inputs/chunk_*.json into verdicts/chunk_*.jsonl
# Follow the atlas-qoder-audit skill and judge/RUBRIC.md

python .qoder/skills/atlas-qoder-audit/scripts/score_verdicts.py my_model
Factual accuracy · grounding + factuality +

An answer passes only when its programmatic grounding check and LLM factuality check both pass. Join completed records by task ID.

BASH / FACTUALITY
export ATLAS_JUDGE_URL='https://your-judge-host.example/v1/chat/completions'
export ATLAS_JUDGE_API_KEY='<your-judge-api-key>'
export ATLAS_JUDGE_MODEL='deepseek-v4-pro'

bash scripts/run_all_factual_accuracy.sh \
  --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model \
  --output judge/factual_accuracy_deepseek_pro/my_model.jsonl

The repository’s combine_passrate_factual.py uses predefined label-to-run mappings for the paper’s configurations. Add your run mapping before using it to aggregate a new model.

Trajectory quality · all four dimensions +

Configure the judge environment as above. Use --dry-run to inspect payloads without API calls; add smoke for a 15-query trial.

BASH / TRAJECTORY JUDGES
bash scripts/run_all_intent_understanding.sh --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model --output judge/intent_understanding_deepseek_pro/my_model.jsonl
bash scripts/run_all_tool_selection.sh --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model --output judge/tool_selection_deepseek_pro/my_model.jsonl
bash scripts/run_all_evidence_sufficiency.sh --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model --output judge/evidence_sufficiency_deepseek_pro/my_model.jsonl
bash scripts/run_all_tool_flexibility.sh --run outputs/my_model.final.jsonl --label my_model --output judge/tool_flexibility_deepseek_pro/my_model.jsonl

python judge/summarize_intent_understanding.py
python judge/summarize_tool_selection.py
python judge/summarize_evidence_sufficiency.py
python judge/summarize_tool_flexibility.py
Execution cost & run comparison +

Tokens, tool calls, and rounds come from telemetry. Compare runs on the same task IDs; audited constraint scores are aggregated separately.

SHELL / COMPARE
python scripts/compare_runs.py \
  --run model_a=outputs/model_a.final.jsonl \
  --run model_b=outputs/model_b.final.jsonl \
  --output outputs/comparison.md
05 / KEEP IT COMPARABLE

Same environment. Auditable differences.

5 rounds≤2 parallel calls per round
≤10 calls in total
100 candidates10 results by default
20 results maximum
Fixed evidencePinned retrieval models
Frozen index build ID
Visible inputs onlyQuery, timestamp, location
No personas or reference targets

Keep prompts, retrieval settings, and the corpus identical. Record reasoning effort, output limits, retries, and any provider-specific deviations alongside each run.
